question: Are those who obey the law cursed?
summary: Deuteronomy 27:26 places under curse anyone who fails to confirm and do all the words of the law, while Galatians 3:10 turns that same verse on its head, claiming that everyone who relies on the works of the law is under a curse.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read the two verses as one point: the law curses any failure to keep it perfectly, so relying on works of the law (which no one fully renders) can only condemn.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, compiling the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, presses the pair at face value: Deuteronomy curses those who do not keep the law, yet Paul says those who are of the works of the law are under a curse.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible ("Are those who obey the law cursed?", skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/cursed.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (contra/cursed.html)

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Galatians 3:10
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact pair directly: his note on Deuteronomy 27:26 sends the reader to his Galatians 3:10 note 'for the reconciliation of these Scriptures,' which argues the curse falls not on doing the law but on the impossibility of doing it perfectly, so reliance on works of the law condemns.

link.title: GotQuestions: What are the works of the law (Romans 3:20; Galatians 2:16)?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment; cites Galatians 3:10 and argues that reliance on the works of the law brings the curse because complete obedience is impossible (the harmonizing move). Does not cite Deut 27:26 by name but squarely engages the core tension.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: for the law requires obedience, and that perfect and constant, and in failure thereof curses, in proof of which the apostle produces this passage … for the reconciliation of these Scriptures, as to what seeming difference there is between them …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill's note on the Deuteronomy verse itself names the apparent conflict ('seeming difference') and frames the harmonization: the law curses failure to keep it, which is exactly what Paul presses in Gal 3:10. Most directly on-tension sentence in the gather. Joined across the internal 'see Gill on Gal 3:10' cross-ref (sense-preserving ellipsis); truncated before the trailing colon-clause -> trailing marker.
excerpts.source_note_text:
Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them,.... That is, who does not perfectly perform all that the law requires, and continues to do so; for the law requires obedience, and that perfect and constant, and in failure thereof curses, in proof of which the apostle produces this passage; see Gill on Gal 3:10, for the reconciliation of these Scriptures, as to what seeming difference there is between them:
and all the people shall say, Amen; See Gill on Deu 27:15; See Gill on Deu 27:16.
